descriptionChirho: A wolf (Canis lupus), the predatory canid used in Scripture both literally and as a figure for violent, rapacious persons or enemies (Gen 49:27 Benjamin as a ravenous wolf; Isa 11:6 wolf dwelling with lamb; Ezek 22:27 princes like wolves; Hab 1:8 swifter than wolves; Zeph 3:3 evening wolves). Translated as English 'wolf/wolves,' Spanish 'lobo/lobos,' Hindi 'bhediya/bhediyon' (भेड़िया/भेड़ियों), Arabic 'dhi'b/dhi'ab' (الذِّئْبُ/ذِئَابُ), Korean 'iri' (이리), Swahili 'mbwa mwitu.' All three clusters represent the same lexeme in different morpho-syntactic frames: absolute, construct, and with prepositions (min, ka).
